qt: to the Commission Ştefan Muşoiu (S&D) Subject:

Linked to over 35 000 deaths a year in the EU/EEA, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the biggest threats to public health in the Union. The EU has already outlined a 2030 strategy for the development of new countermeasures against AMR, which will be financed to the tune of EUR 30 million under the EU4Health programme. 1.

In the light of these objectives and the fact that HERA has identified certain vulnerabilities in the antibiotic supply chain and a limited production capacity for certain active pharmaceutical ingredients in the EU, will the Commission provide funding to bolster the Union’s production capacities for antibiotics and active pharmaceutical ingredients with a view to reducing its dependence on external suppliers?

Will the Commission also support the establishment, including through European funding, of integrated centres of excellence for antimicrobial resistance that combine research, rapid diagnoses, the development of new antibiotics, the production of active ingredients and the building up of strategic reserves, particularly in Member States with low pharmaceutical production capacity?

Last but not least, given that the tendency to use antibiotics in a cautious manner limits sales volumes and, as a result, makes it difficult to financially sustain the development of new antibiotics, what push and pull mechanisms does the Commission intend to use to incentivise the development of new antibiotics by the European pharmaceutical and biotech sectors?
